rules.body: Apply this rule where observers share persistent query state, cancellation resources belong to individual fetches, consumption is recorded on actual signal access, and continuation is deferred. README.md: "Multiple observers share one fetch." README.md: "Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller\nand completion." README.md: "paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn."

After the final observer leaves a fresh online-mode attempt mounted entirely offline, prevent reconnect from entering its signal-consuming query function with a live signal. This must hold independently of refetchOnReconnect. TASK: "Repair the rail timetable lookup cache: a fresh online-mode query mounted and unmounted entirely offline later calls its signal-consuming query function with a live signal after reconnect. This occurs independently of refetchOnReconnect."

Check cancellation against both future continuation scheduling and callbacks already deferred. The public implementation schedules via src/Workflow.java: "env.call(\"defer\",token);" and checks attempt identity and settlement through "boolean active(Query q,Attempt a){return q.attempt==a&&!a.settled;}". Verify that an abandoned attempt cannot regain permission to enter when its deferred callback runs.

Preserve the distinction between shared signal-consumption bookkeeping and attempt-owned cancellation resources. README.md: "Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller\nand completion." src/Workflow.java: "int getter=env.bind(x->{q.consumed=true;return null;});". A repair must continue recording actual lazy access rather than treating observer departure or paused status as signal consumption.

Do not generalize abandonment of fresh offline work into cancellation of every observerless or paused fetch. README.md: "Unconsumed active work can finish into cache\nafter its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable." Check entered unconsumed work separately from the target never-entered attempt, and examine cached background continuation before extending the cancellation condition.

Preserve sharing, inert unknown departures, cancellation restoration, and attempt isolation. README.md: "Multiple observers share one fetch." README.md: "Cancellation\nreverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late\nfulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert." Verify remaining observers, consumed cancellation, observer reuse, and late completion after a replacement attempt.

Verify timing and eligibility separately from abandonment: synchronous initial online entry, asynchronous completion and paused continuation, network modes, focus gating, and scheduled retries. README.md: "Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn." README.md: "First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles."

Keep repairs within product source and retain supported interfaces and build behavior. TASK: "Preserve supported query behavior, interfaces, dependencies and build/test configuration. Change product source only."

limitations: The supplied static analysis reports unsupported Java coverage; it does not prove execution order, aliasing, or cancellation correctness.
The three reported passing public examples establish only those observations. They do not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.
TASK does not prescribe an implementation strategy or resolve whether entry with an already-aborted signal is acceptable.
The public source has no refetchOnReconnect branch. Independence from that option is required by TASK, but a new option implementation is not required.
The proposed started flag and null-data condition are candidate implementation choices, not reusable business requirements.
The public documents do not exhaustively specify every cached paused-work scenario; preservation checks must distinguish documented behavior from inferred policy.
